news.title: U-17 Women’s World Cup 2026: How Nigeria ending North Korea’s 18-match unbeaten run can inspire African women’s football
news.lede: Nigeria’s 3–1 victory over defending champions DPR Korea did more than secure a place in the Round of 16 on Friday. It ended an extraordinary unbeaten run and reminded Africa that its young footballers can challenge the world’s most accomplished teams. Nigeria’s Flamingos did not just defeat the defending champions at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco. They brought an end to a remarkable run of dominance and delivered a statement that should resonate across African women’s football.

news.title: Rugby League World Cup 2026: England 'not thinking about points difference' before France game, says Brad O'Neill
news.lede: England hooker Brad O'Neill says his side will resist the urge to go for broke when they face France in their second Rugby League World Cup match in Perth on Saturday. An opening 30-12 defeat to Tonga has left their hopes of reaching the semi-finals hanging by a thread, with points difference looking increasingly like the only way to progress. But head coach Brian McDermott has named an unchanged 19-man matchday squad, a sign that he does not plan radical changes against a France team smarting from their 78-4 humbling by Samoa. What did we learn from England in the first round of RLWC 2026?

news.title: FIFA U15 World Cup: Malta lose to Kenya in opening match
news.lede: Malta lost 2-6 to Kenya in the first match from the FIFA U15 World Cup & Festival being held at the Hovsan Competition Complex in Azerbaijan. Kenya took the lead thanks to Innocent Media on 5 minutes and Lewis Wafula doubled the score three minutes later. An own goal extended the lead for the African side on 15 minutes and Duncan Muyah made it 4-0. Malta hit back with two penalties by Declan Zammit on 25 minutes and Enzo De Freitas on 29 minutes but Kenya added another two goals thanks to Silas Juma on 32 minutes and Muyah four minutes later.

news.title: Infantino says he has backing of most of football world — Anadolu Agency
news.lede: After the FIFA Council meeting held on October 15 in Zurich, Switzerland, the organization’s president Gianni Infantino said he has the backing of the “vast, vast majority” of the football world. In an interview with BBC Sport, he also dismissed questions about a possible resignation after the withdrawal of a controversial proposal to transfer part of FIFA’s commercial rights to a private investment firm. Infantino said that disagreements in world football are normal, but after discussing different positions, it is necessary to move on. Calls for his resignation intensified two months ago amid the dispute over the FIFA Forward Enterprise project.

news.title: Azerbaijan U-15 national football team makes flying start at World Cup in Baku
news.lede: The Azerbaijan U-15 national football team opened the FIFA U-15 World Cup and Festival in Baku in a commanding fashion as they beat Timor-Leste 6–0 on Saturday, APA reports. Azerbaijan took complete control of the match, with double strikes from Mushfig Zamanov and Hasan Mahmadov setting the tone before Yusif Alizada and Asif Allahverdizada also found the net to cap off a flawless opening performance at the Baky Crystal Hall. The national team will play their next match against Andorra on October 24. The first matches of the tournament kicked off on October 23.

news.title: Gianni Infantino laughs off calls to quit as FIFA president despite World Cup commercial rights storm
news.lede: Gianni Infantino has defiantly dismissed suggestions that he should resign from his post as FIFA president following a period of intense institutional turmoil. The Swiss-Italian administrator claims he retains the overwhelming support of the global football community despite facing a backlash over plans to sell off commercial rights.Infantino survives commercial rights falloutTwo months ago, Infantino faced immense pressure from UEFA, CONCACAF, and the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) . The confederation heads accused him of 'deception' regarding the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) initiative. This controversial proposal involved selling a share of FIFA's commercial rights to a private investment firm.Infantino abandoned the FFE project just days after its introduction.
